q: A factor map π: (X,σ) → (Y,σ) between subshifts is analogous to a noisy channel because:
opts: It may be many-to-one: multiple inputs produce the same output (like noise obscuring the input)
It always reduces entropy by exactly H(X)-H(Y)
exp: A factor map is like a noisy channel: the output y=π(x) may not uniquely determine x (it is many-to-one in general). The 'noise' is the hidden information in the fibre π⁻¹(y). Entropy decreases: h_top(Y) ≤ h_top(X), and h_μ(Y) = h_μ(X) - h_μ(X|Y).
